blocks.content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of India. It regulates the country's monetary system and manages the currency and credit system of the economy. It plays a vital role in maintaining financial stability and controlling inflation.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission.
RBI was nationalized on January 1, 1949, transforming it from a private shareholders' bank to a fully government-owned central bank.
Serves as the issuer of currency notes (except one-rupee notes and coins) and acts as the banker to both the Central/State governments and commercial banks.
Formulates and implements monetary policy using direct and indirect instruments including Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, CRR, SLR, and Open Market Operations.
The Central Board of Directors, headed by the Governor and supported by Deputy Governors, governs the overall affairs of the bank.

blocks.content: • It was established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
• The headquarters of RBI is located in Mumbai.
• To regulate the issue of banknotes.
• To maintain monetary stability in the country.
• To operate the currency and credit system.
The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935 in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

cells: RBI issues currency notes except one-rupee note.
RBI manages accounts of central and state governments.

blocks.content: • Repo Rate – Rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks.
• Reverse Repo Rate – Rate at which RBI borrows money from banks.
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) – Percentage of deposits banks must keep with RBI.
• Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) – Percentage of deposits banks must maintain in liquid assets.

rows: Regulates the total volume of money supply and credit in the economy.
Regulates the allocation and direction of credit to specific sectors.
Includes Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, CRR, SLR, and Open Market Operations.
Includes Margin Requirements, Moral Suasion, Credit Rationing, and Direct Action.
Applies uniformly across all sectors of the financial system.
Targeted selectively to discourage or encourage credit in specific industries.

blocks.content: • Open Market Operations – Buying and selling government securities.
• Central Board of Directors – Governing body.

items: Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor of the RBI, while C.D. Deshmukh was the first Indian Governor.
One-rupee notes and coins bear the signature of the Finance Secretary and are issued by the Ministry of Finance, not the RBI.
Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is maintained strictly in cash with the RBI, whereas Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is maintained by banks with themselves in liquid assets.
The headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India was permanently moved from Kolkata to Mumbai in 1937.

blocks.content: • RBI issues all currency notes except one-rupee note.
